result: UFMTrack achieves 90% track reconstruction efficiency, eliminates experimenter bias, performs comparably to experienced manual analysis, and reduces analysis time by factors of 3-5 compared to manual methods.
evaluation: All three reviewers affirm the utility and accuracy of the algorithm. Reviewer 1 states 'the algorithm is almost as accurate as manual tracking and importantly saves time for researchers.' Reviewer 2 appreciates 'the comparison between manual and software analysis' and notes the tool provides 'opportunity to unify the data and results.' The editor describes the framework as 'convincing.' No concerns are raised about these performance claims.

result: The 2D+T model outperformed the 2D model by 9% for T-cell mask prediction and by 32% for transmigration mask prediction, though the 2D+T model was sensitive to frame misalignment causing false positives.
evaluation: Reviewers do not question the model performance comparisons or the technical details of the segmentation approach. The editor describes the framework as 'convincing' for visualizing and tracking immune cells, implicitly accepting these technical performance metrics.

result: UFMTrack detected statistically significant differences in T-cell motility parameters under different cytokine stimulation conditions, including detachment kinetics, crawling speeds, meandering index, and effects on transmigrated cells, with results consistent with previous manual analyses.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these biological findings. The editor notes the work 'elucidates how immune cells migrate across the blood brain barrier' and describes the framework as 'convincing,' implicitly accepting the biological insights generated by the tool. Reviewer 2 notes the assay's reproducibility and stability are important achievements.

result: Automated analysis agreed with experienced manual analysis but revealed significant errors in manual tracking (jittery patterns, overestimated crawling speeds), highlighted experimenter variability, and demonstrated that manual analysis requires 8-13 hours per dataset compared to 2.3 hours for automation.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly appreciates 'the comparison between manual and software analysis.' Reviewer 1 affirms 'the algorithm is almost as accurate as manual tracking and importantly saves time.' No reviewer questions the comparison methodology or the finding that automation improves accuracy over manual methods.

result: UFMTrack successfully generalized to different cell types (human PBMCs, macrophages, human T cells) and endothelial cell types (HBMEC, EECM-BMECs), detecting cells of varying sizes and confirming previously reported biological findings, though transmigration detection for macrophages required additional training.
evaluation: The editor emphasizes the framework can 'visualize, recognize and track the movement of different immune cells across primary human and mouse brain microvascular endothelial cells,' directly affirming the generalizability claims. Reviewers raise no concerns about the cross-species or cross-cell-type applications.

result: Manual analysis of in vitro flow assays is time-consuming, prone to errors and subjective judgments, limits statistical power, and is hampered by technical challenges of phase contrast imaging with unlabeled cells.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 acknowledges 'there is currently no clear software analysis program, and many labs have their own methods,' validating the problem statement. Reviewer 1 notes the algorithm 'saves time for researchers,' implicitly accepting the limitations of manual analysis. No reviewer disputes these characterizations of manual methods.

result: Existing tracking toolkits are unsuitable for detecting distinct migration regimes and cell interactions, and none consider migration under flow causing rapid cell displacement; UFMTrack addresses these gaps by enabling detection of crawling, probing, transmigration, and accelerated movement.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 states 'the authors have discussed how their tool compares to other tracking methods,' and no concerns are raised about the novelty claims. Reviewer 2 notes 'there is currently no clear software analysis program' for this application, supporting the claim that existing tools are inadequate.

result: UFMTrack has limitations including reduced performance at high cell densities (>250 cells/dataset), inability to detect cell division (though this occurs rarely, <1% of T cells), and recommended cell concentration of 100-150 k/ml.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these stated limitations. The transparent acknowledgment of limitations is consistent with the overall positive reception of the work, and no reviewer suggests these limitations undermine the tool's utility.

result: UFMTrack contributes to the 3R principle by reducing animal use and has potential applications in fundamental research, pharmaceutical screening, personalized medicine, cancer metastasis studies, and real-time operation.
evaluation: The editor states the work 'will be of broad interest to the cancer biology, immunology and medical therapeutics fields,' affirming the broad applicability claims. Reviewers do not question these potential applications, treating them as reasonable extensions of the demonstrated capabilities.

result: Background claims about BBB function, immune cell extravasation as a multistep process, T-cell behaviors (crawling, probing, diapedesis), and clinical translation of BBB research.
evaluation: These are established background claims supported by citations. The editor affirms the work 'elucidates how immune cells migrate across the blood brain barrier,' accepting the biological context. No reviewer questions these foundational concepts.

result: Observational claims about T-cell behavior under flow: cells instantly appear in the field of view and are often suddenly displaced or detached during the assay.
evaluation: These are descriptive observations of the experimental system. Reviewer 2 acknowledges the challenge of including 'physiological flow' in the assay, implicitly accepting these flow-related phenomena. No concerns are raised about these observations.

result: Methodological details including cell isolation, stimulation protocols, flow conditions, imaging parameters, dataset structure, and model architecture specifications.
evaluation: Reviewers do not question the experimental methods or technical implementation details. Reviewer 2 notes 'it is quite a challenge to get this assay reproducible and stable,' acknowledging the methodological rigor required, and no concerns are raised about the described methods.
